subject: babaYagaHut
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs.
Style: Slavic folk art.

spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut
spec.description: A folk-art diorama of Baba Yaga's log hut standing on two giant chicken legs on a round earth plinth, with a skull fence, a painted carved gable and a glowing window.
spec.layout: Front is +Z. A round earth plinth (radius 3.3, top at y=0.25) is the diorama base. On it stands the hut on two big yellow chicken legs (x=±0.9), toes spread forward and one back toe, with feathered orange thigh puffs under the floor. The log cabin is a 3.2 x 3.2 m square (x,z ±1.6 including notched corner log ends), floor at y=1.8, walls up to y=3.8, and it faces +Z. The door is centred on the front wall. A small porch deck and a steep stair come out of the door and run down to the plinth at z≈3.0, between the legs. A steep gable roof with its ridge along Z, eaves at y=3.75 and ridge at y≈5.2, has carved horse-head 'konyok' finials at both ridge ends, a painted front gable (fronton) with a sun rosette and a round glowing window, and a brick chimney on the right-back with smoke puffs. A ring of bone-pale skulls on pointed stakes fences the plinth edge (radius 2.9) from the back round to both sides, with a gap in front for the stair. Mushrooms, grass tufts, a mortar and a broom sit near the edge. Slavic folk art style: bold flat colour, a limited red, gold, blue, teal, cream and black palette. Everything is outlined or trimmed in contrasting small parts: carved zigzag and comb bargeboards, rosettes, stylised tulips and rooster motifs painted as small parts on the trim, the gable and the shutters. The wood is warm brown with pale cut log ends. The proportions are chunky and slightly toy-like, and the legs are oversized and characterful. Every part uses the shared motifs: the 8-petal sun rosette (gold centre, red petals, white dots), the zigzag border (red/white) and the tulip (red with green leaves).

parts.builds: The diorama ground on joint ground. A low faceted round plinth (radius 3.3, y 0 to 0.25, about 14 sides) in earth, with a slightly smaller grass-coloured top disc and darker earth rim stones around the edge. Scatter grass tufts (grass / grassLight cones and blades) over the top, and a few folk-style flowers (folkRed or folkGold petals, folkGreen stem). The skull fence: about 14 stakes (logDark pointed posts, 1.1 to 1.4 m tall, leaning slightly) on a circle of radius 2.9 covering the whole circle except the front gap within ±28° of +Z (the stair). Each stake is topped with a bone skull (sphere cranium, small box jaw, dark eye sockets) and about half of the skulls have glowWarm eyes. Short crossbars of logMid join neighbouring stakes at y≈0.7. Also: three or four fly-agaric mushrooms (folkRed caps with folkWhite dots, folkWhite stems) near the back-left of the plinth, a small mortar (stone lathe) with a pestle at the right front (x≈2.0, z≈1.8), a besom broom leaning on the fence at the left (logLight handle, featherLight twig bundle bound with folkRed), and a stump. Keep everything out of the area under the hut (|x|<1.8, |z|<1.8) except the legs' own footprints and the stair at x≈0, z 2.1 to 3.0. Nothing may rise above y=1.6.
parts.attaches: Top face at mount plinthTop (y=0.25): the legs' toes rest on it and the stair ends on it at stairFoot. Rides joint ground.

parts.builds: The two giant chicken legs, mirrored in x, rigged on hipL/kneeL/ankleL/footL/toes (and the R equivalents) at the positions in the joints list; thighs are a little forward-angled and the shins plunge down to the foot, a bird rest pose with all four toes separated. Each leg has a big feathered thigh puff (a cluster of overlapping featherOrange and featherLight teardrop blades or flattened spheres, 12–18 per leg, hanging from the hip under the cabin floor at y≈1.4–1.85), a legYellow tubular upper shin and a lower tarsus with stacked legScale scale ridges (small flat plates or rings, 6–8 per tarsus), a bulging knee/ankle joint knob, and a rear spur (small claw cone). The foot has three front toes (mid, in, out) and one back toe, each a tapering legYellow tube made of two or three segments with knuckle bumps and legScale scutes on top, ending in a thick curved claw cone (claw colour) pressing on the plinth top. Toes lie almost flat at y≈0.28–0.4 and fan out in a clear 'bird foot'. The hip tops are hidden under the cabin sill at y 1.8–1.9. Also add two thick folkRed painted ankle bands (rings) as the folk-art accent on each tarsus. The legs must be oversized, chunky and characterful, with the thigh puff about 0.5 m wide.
parts.attaches: Hips at mounts legHipL/legHipR touch the underside of cabinSill (y=1.8); feet at footL/footR rest on plinthTop. The stair at x≈0 passes between the legs, so keep the inner toes at |x|>=0.45.

parts.builds: The log cabin body on joint hut, from the sill at y=1.8 to the eaves line at y=3.8. A sill frame of two layers of thick logDark logs at y 1.8–1.95 (floor top at 1.95). Walls are stacked horizontal round logs (radius ≈0.125, 8 courses) on all four sides, alternating logMid / logLight / logDark. The log ends project 0.12 beyond each corner in a notched crossing pattern, each end capped with a pale logEnd disc with a darker ring detail. The front wall faces +Z at z=1.5. A centred door (width 0.95, y 1.95 to 3.45) made of vertical planks in logMid with folkBlue painted panels, folkGold iron straps and hinges, a round folkGold handle and a folkRed tulip painted on each panel; the door frame is carved logLight with a zigzag red/white border. Above the door sit lintel logs up to the eaves. Two small windows flank the door on the front wall (x=±1.05, y 2.75 to 3.3, glowWarm glass with folkBlack cross muntins) with carved nalichniki frames (folkWhite carved boards with folkRed zigzag and little folkBlue rosettes) and folkTeal shutters painted with folkGold stars. Each side wall (x=±1.5) has a larger window (z≈0.1, y 2.6 to 3.4) with the same carved frame, shutters and a flower box with tulips. The back wall has one round-top window with shutters. Window glass is glowWarm. The top plate at y≈3.8 carries cross-log ends. Every wall detail is a seated small part in its own colour. The cabin's inner volume is a box core in logDark (hidden behind the logs) so that no gaps show.
parts.attaches: Sits on the legs at cabinSill (y=1.8). The porch connects at doorCentre (front wall z=1.6 including log ends) and cabinFloorTop. The roof sits on the eavesLine (y=3.8). Rides joint hut.

parts.builds: The porch and stair on joint hut, in front of the door. A porch deck of planks (logLight / logMid alternating boards) from z=1.6 to z=2.2 at y 1.8 to 1.95, x ±1.1, with end-grain beams under it. Two carved posts (logDark with folkRed and folkGold bands, bulb tops) at x=±1.05, z=2.15 rise to 3.3 and hold a small shed canopy (a tilted board roof, y 3.25 to 3.6, z 1.6 to 2.4, shingle strips in shingleTeal and shingleBlue with a folkRed carved zigzag edge board). A balustrade of turned balusters (folkWhite with folkRed caps) with a logMid handrail on both sides of the deck and of the stair, height 0.7 above the tread. A steep stair of 7 plank treads (logLight, with folkRed front edge strips) descends from the deck front edge (porchDeckFront, y 1.95, z 2.2) to stairFoot (y 0.25, z 3.0), x ±0.45, with two logDark stringers. The stair sits between the legs, so keep clear of |x|>0.55 below y=1.9. Hanging details on the canopy and posts: a string of folkWhite onion-like bulbs on a rope, a string of dried red mushrooms, bunches of herbs (folkGreen, folkGold), and a skull lantern (bone skull with glowWarm eyes) hanging from the canopy at x=-0.9. A small folkBlue-and-folkRed painted rooster plaque on the canopy front board, made from small extruded parts.
parts.attaches: Deck back edge meets the cabin front wall at doorCentre (z≈1.6); stair foot rests at stairFoot on plinthTop. The canopy stays below the roof's front eave at y≈3.75.

parts.builds: The steep gable roof and everything above the eaves on joint hut. Two roof slopes made of overlapping shingle rows (alternating shingleTeal and shingleBlue scalloped rows with folkRed edging on every third row) meeting at the ridge (y≈5.2, ridge along Z, z from -2.2 to 2.2), the eaves at y 3.75 with half-width 2.1 at the sides, front and back overhang to z=±2.3. A thick logDark ridge log with a carved folkGold zigzag. At each ridge end a horse-head finial (konyok), a chunky stylised carved horse head about 0.6 m tall in logLight with a folkRed mane, folkGold eye and folkBlack nostril, built from small extrudes and boxes. The front gable (fronton, triangle at z≈2.0, from y 3.8 to 5.1) is vertical planks in logMid with a large 8-petal sun rosette (folkGold centre, folkRed petals, folkWhite dot border) around a round glowWarm window (radius 0.28) framed in folkWhite carved board. On both sides of the rosette, folkBlue tulip and folkGreen leaf motifs. Carved bargeboards (pritselina) run along the front and back rake edges, lace-cut folkWhite boards with folkRed comb teeth and folkBlue circles hanging below, with a pendant (podvesa) at the bottom of the gable. The back gable is simpler: planks with a small rosette. Rafter ends in logDark under the eaves on both sides. A brick-red chimney (folkRed bricks, folkBlack top, a stone cap) at chimneyBase (x=0.9, z=-0.9) rising through the slope to y≈5.5, with four rounded smoke puffs (smoke colour, spheres getting bigger) rising to y≈5.8. Small moss clumps (grass) along the lower shingle rows.
parts.attaches: Rests on the cabin top plate at eavesLine (y=3.8); the front gable base is at frontGableBase; ridge finials at ridgeFront and ridgeBack; chimney at chimneyBase. Rides joint hut. The porch canopy sits below the front eave.

calls.reasoning:
I'm weighing whether a Baba Yaga hut on chicken legs should be static or rigged, and I'm leaning toward a simple rig with joints at the legs so it can move. I need the builders to agree on the joint layout, so I'm starting to define a root at the hut floor with the spine and left and right leg joints.

I'm settling the joint chains for the legs, hip, knee and ankle on each side, with the cabin riding on the hut root. I'm also sizing the hut at roughly 3.0 by 3.4 meters, with the legs resting on a small round forest-floor base that has a skull fence and a ladder.

I'm laying out the rest of the hut: a log-pile underfloor and notched log walls, then a steep gable roof with a carved horse-head ridge, a folk-art sun pediment, and window frames. The cabin will also get a door, painted shutters, a porch with steps, and a chimney. For the base I'm planning a round earth plinth of about 3.2 meters radius with a skull fence, fly agaric mushrooms, ferns, a stump, a bucket, a broom, and a mortar and pestle, keeping it tight.

I'm working out the cabin's proportions: legs up to about 1.85 meters, the floor sitting at 1.9, walls running to 3.9, and the gable roof climbing to roughly 5.3 with a horse-head ridge at each end. I'm also sorting out how the front door gets down to the ground, which means a steep wooden stair or ladder reaching from the porch to the base near the front.

I'm placing the porch at the front of the cabin, around 1.9 to 2.9 meters out, with a rail, and running the stairs down the center between the legs. The legs sit at roughly ±0.9 on x, with the toes spreading forward and back, so an 0.9-meter-wide stair should clear them.

I'm placing the hut's hip joints near the middle of the legs, with the knee joints pushed out and forward so the chicken-leg shape reads clearly.

I'm placing the hip, knee, and ankle joints for each chicken leg, with the ankle acting as the hock, and I'm putting the foot ground center just forward of it. The main root for the hut sits at the middle of the cabin floor, with the legs hanging from it.

I'm working out how to give the base its own placement, since the only root joint is the hut's and the plinth shouldn't travel with it. I'm checking whether I can keep it static without adding a second root.

I'm setting up a ground root at the origin and hanging the hut root from it at the cabin height, with the legs chaining off the hut and the base riding the ground. Next I'm choosing the palette: log browns from dark to light, a teal-and-red shingle pattern, and folk-art red and gold for the carving.

I'm writing out the color palette now: log browns, folk-art reds, golds, blues and teals, with yellow and orange for the chicken legs and a glowing gold for the eyes.

I'm pinning down the mount points: the ground top at y=0.25, the hut root at 1.8, and the cabin walls running from 1.8 up to 3.8 with the eaves at 3.8 and the roof reaching 5.3. I'm settling on a door height of about 1.5 meters, with the porch deck top at 1.95.

I'm now specifying the base diorama: a plinth with grass, a partial skull fence on the back and sides, mushrooms, flowers, a mortar and broom, with a gap near the front for the stairs. Then I'm setting up the legs part, with a budget of about 180.

I'm splitting the hut into five parts now: the base, the legs, the cabin walls with door and windows, the roof with its pediment and chimney, and the porch with its stairs. The legs part gets the joint chains and the toe detail, and the base stays on its own ground root so it doesn't move with the hut.

I'm boxing in the porch and its stairs: the deck runs out from the cabin front, with the stairs dropping to the ground, and a canopy sits over the door. I'm also checking the bounding boxes for the cabin, porch, and parts budget to keep the total under the limit.

I'm finishing the porch's bounding box and the roof dimensions, with the ridge around y 5.2 and a chimney on one side. The whole model comes to about 5.7 tall, and I'm checking that a 6.6 by 6.6 footprint clears the plinth at radius 3.3.

I'm checking the front porch canopy and its supports so they clear the roof overhang, with the canopy slab sitting around y 3.3 to 3.6 under the eaves. I'm also settling the folk-art styling: bold flat colors in red, gold, blue, and teal, with carved sun rosettes, comb patterns, zigzag trim, tulips, and a rooster. For the log walls I'm stacking eight courses of horizontal cylinders with a radius of about 0.125.

I'm placing the door on the front wall, centered and about 0.9 meters wide, rising to roughly 3.45. I'm weighing whether to put windows on the front too, but the porch railing would cover them, so I'm leaning toward moving them to the sides instead.

I'm sketching out the front-facing details now: the flanking windows at about x ±1.05, the railing height, and the shutters. Next I'm laying out the mount points, the palette, and the joint directions for the hut and the hip joints.

I'm placing the ankle and foot joints for each leg, with the toes sitting just above the plinth top at about y 0.33.

I'm defining the toe joints for each foot, with a middle toe pointing forward, two splayed toes angled in and out, and a back toe. Then I'm checking the leg bounding box so the toes and thigh feathers stay within bounds.

I'm settling the overall size at about 5.8 meters tall, with the roof ridge near 5.2, the konyok ends reaching 5.5, and the chimney topping out around 5.4 with smoke puffs rising to 5.8. That sets the roof bounding box top at 5.8.
